key_insight: The paper provides the first direct experimental observation of Kelvin-wave turbulence along a single vortex filament, confirming a weak-turbulence cascade driven by six-wave resonant interactions.
engineering_relevance: This advances understanding of energy transport in vortex-core dynamics, with implications for modeling and controlling turbulence in both classical and quantum flow systems.
method: High-resolution spatiotemporal measurements of a single vortex filament
Spectral analysis of Kelvin-wave amplitude across multiple scales
Comparison with weak-turbulence predictions and resonant-interaction theory
evidence_signal: The measured wave-amplitude spectra match the predicted weak-turbulence cascade and support six-wave resonant energy transfer.
watch_item: The findings are based on a controlled single-vortex experiment, so extending them to more complex or multi-vortex flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Experimental evidence of Kelvin wave turbulence along a vortex core
